# Apocalypse of Peter — Chapter 2
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Source:** Akhmim Fragment / Ethiopic MS, Apocalypse of Peter 2

---

1. We — his apostles — pressed him: "Lord, tell us what is coming. What will we see? How are we supposed to understand the resurrection of the dead? You are telling us extraordinary things."

2. The Lord showed us a vast garden, overflowing with beautiful trees, with blessed fruit, with the fragrance of perfumes drifting on the air. The scent was exquisite — it reached us where we stood.

3. He also showed me an ancient man, blazing white, and said: "This is what it will look like when their hour of need comes."

4. I said: "Lord, I don't understand. Who is this ancient man? Who are the children? What is this place?"

5. He said to me: "This garden — these trees — they are the righteous dead. All the beautiful things you see here belong to those who died for the sake of righteousness.

6. The ancient man you saw is Moses. He represents the law that God gave him on Mount Sinai.

7. And the children — they are the ones who died young, before they had ever sinned, before they reached the age when sin becomes possible. They are in God's own keeping."

8. Then he said: "I will show you something else — another mystery. When God judges the world, the righteous will stand at his right hand and the sinners at his left.

9. But notice: some of the righteous will shine and some will not. Because some sinned and some did not."

10. I said: "I don't understand. Explain this to me."

11. He said: "Those who shine — they are the ones who never sinned, who lived entirely by God's will. Those who don't shine — they sinned, but they turned back to God at the end of their lives.

12. Among the righteous there were some who chose poverty in this world for God's sake. Some fasted. Some prayed without stopping. Some gave everything they had.

13. All of this will be made plain at the resurrection — everything according to God's own design.

14. And all of them will receive what God has prepared for those who fear him: a kingdom, honor, and glory without end."

---
*PNEUMA note: The garden vision is rendered as an unfolding experience, drawing the reader into the visionary's perspective. The Moses identification is preserved as given in the text.*
